title: NSAT General Mock Test 01
description: Complete NSAT General mock test #1 with realistic exam experience. 80 questions across 6 sections.
instructions: Marking scheme: +4 for correct, -1 for incorrect
Answer all questions - no optional sections
Test is proctored via webcam and microphone

questions.questionText: When Meena was as old as Anuj is now, the ratio of their ages was ⁠<inlineMath>4:3⁠</inlineMath>.When Anuj’s age becomes equal to the present age of Meena, what will be the ratio of their ages at that time?

Examine the following statements regarding the equation <inlineMath>{\left( {{x^2} + 2} \right)^2} + 8{x^2} = 6x\left( {{x^2} + 2} \right)</inlineMath>. 

I. All the roots of the equation are complex.
II. The total sum of all the roots of the equation is equal to 6.

Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?

In a botanical garden, the number of rose plants, tulip plants, and sunflower plants is <inlineMath>3:7:5</inlineMath>. If the difference between the number of tulip plants and rose plants is divisible by both 3 and 7, what is the minimum possible total number of these plants in the garden?

Rohan invests Rs 10,000 by dividing the amount between two fixed deposit plans, Plan X and Plan Y. Plan X offers compound interest at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly. Plan Y offers simple interest at 12% per annum. At the end of one year, the return from Plan Y exceeds the return from Plan X by Rs 2,310. What is the total interest earned by Rohan from both plans at the end of the year?
Consider a quadratic equation |x - 3|2 + |x - 3| - 3 =0 such that the roots of this equation are real. Find the sum of all real roots.

Rahul and Sohan each bought a smartphone at the same price. Later, Aman purchased both smartphones at equal prices from Rahul and Sohan. However, Rahul made a profit of a%, while Sohan's profit percentage was b%. Since Sohan calculated his profit on the selling price, it is given that of a. If Aman later sells one of the smartphones to Deepak at a% profit, what would be the cost price for Deepak, given that Aman purchased each smartphone for Rs 24,000?

There are ten book shelves in a school library, with an average of 50 books on each shelf. Every shelf has a minimum of 42 books, and no two shelves have the same number of books. How many books is the most that can fit on a single shelf?

A cricket academy wants to purchase 100 training items for exactly Rs 10,000. They can buy cones at Rs 200 each, skipping ropes at Rs 50 each, and whistles at Rs 10 each. The academy must buy at least one of each item and cannot purchase any other type of equipment. In how many distinct ways can the academy make this purchase?

In a competitive cricket league with 15 teams labeled Team A through Team O, each team played every other team exactly once in a single round-robin format. Teams received 3 points for a win, 2 points for a draw/cancelled match, and 1 point for a loss. Team M secured the highest number of points and topped the table, while Team E ended with the lowest score of 21 points. Each team finished with a distinct total score. It is also known that Team M had at least one match that ended in a draw or was cancelled. Which of the following must always be true about Team M's performance?

options.text: Team M had at least two draws/cancelled matches
Team M had no more than 3 losses
Team M won no more than 9 matches

questions.questionText: The prices of two commodities are in the ratio of 3:4. If the price of the first commodity is increased by p % and the price of the second commodity is decreased by 25%, then the new prices become in the ratio of 7:5. What is the value of p?

When it comes to completing work, Arun is considered to be four times more efficient than Bankul. Arun can complete a task in 45 days faster than Bankul could if he did it alone. For the first 12 days, Bankul works alone on the task. After 12 days, Arun joins Bankul and they both together complete the remaining part of the work. How many days (approx. ) in total will it take to finish the whole work?

Two cyclists, Arjun and Varun, are training on two circular tracks. The radius of track A is 150 m, and the radius of track B is 30 m, which touch each other at point P. Arjun rides at a speed of 30 km/h on track A, while Varun rides at a speed of 10 km/h on track B. If they start from point P at the same time, after how many complete rounds will Arjun make before he meets Varun again at point P for the first time?

Ravi deposited an amount of Rs <inlineMath>x</inlineMath> in a bank for 2 years at a compound interest rate of 12% per annum. Meanwhile, Neha deposited Rs <inlineMath>\left( {x + 1,500} \right)</inlineMath> in another bank for 3 years at a simple interest rate of 8% per annum. If the amount of interest earned by both of them is the same, what is the amount initially deposited by Ravi?

A and B are two workers assigned to complete a task together. Worker A can complete the task in 15 hours working alone, while Worker B can complete the same task in x hours working alone. After working together for 5 hours, A leaves, and B continues alone to finish the remaining task. If the total time taken to complete the task is exactly 20 hours, what is the value of x?
A box has 6 different locks and 6 keys, only one for each lock. The keys are shuffled randomly. Find the probability that exactly 2 keys open their correct locks.

In a Costume Design Studio, each costume is uniquely made using three features:

  • Fabric Type: One of 5 options — Silk, Wool, Cotton, Velvet, or Linen
  • Sleeve Style: One of 2 options — Long or Short
  • Mask Type: One of 3 options — Animal, Robot, or Human

So, each costume is defined by a combination of these three attributes: fabric, sleeve style, and mask type.

A matching ensemble is a group of three different costumes that follow this special rule:

For each attribute (fabric, sleeve, and mask), the values in the three costumes must be either:

  • All the same (e.g., all have long sleeves), or
  • All different (e.g., one has Silk, one Wool, one Cotton).

Costumes where an attribute has two same and one different value (e.g., two long sleeves and one Short) are not allowed in a matching ensemble.

How many such matching ensembles are possible?

A mobile phone manufacturing company sells five different brands, and the sales distribution for the year 2024 is shown in the pie chart below. The total number of mobile phones sold is 80,000.

 

 

The selling price per unit for each brand is as follows:

Samsung = ₹55,000

Xiaomi = ₹32,000

 

If Samsung discontinues its sales, how many Xiaomi phones must be sold to match Samsung's revenue?

A car is moving along a straight road. It passes point A with a speed of 20 m/s. The driver sees a red traffic signal 200 meters ahead at point B and immediately starts decelerating uniformly to come to a stop exactly at the signal.
However, 3 seconds after the car starts decelerating, a motorcycle passes point A moving in the same direction with a constant speed of 25 m/s.
At what distance from point A will the motorcycle catch up with the car?
The car’s deceleration is found from the equation of motion:
<inlineMath>{v^2} = {u^2} + 2as</inlineMath>
u and v are the initial and final velocities
a is the acceleration and s is the distance.
The car’s position is found from the formula:
<inlineMath>x(t) = ut + \frac{1}{2}a{t^2}</inlineMath>
u is the initial velocity, t is the time, and a is the acceleration

In Aryan's team, there are 8 colleagues—P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, and W—working in different roles: Project Manager, Analyst, Designer, Tester, Developer, Consultant, HR, and Accountant (not necessarily in the same order). They decide to hold a meeting and sit in a circular arrangement. Aryan is observing their seating arrangement. Here are some clues:

  1. P sits to the immediate left of the Tester and is not the Developer.
  2. The HR sits one place away from the Designer but does not sit next to the Consultant.
  3. W, who is the Analyst, is seated opposite the Project Manager.
  4. Q is the HR and sits between the Accountant and the Consultant.
  5. T is the Developer and sits to the immediate right of S.
  6. V is the Designer and sits next to the Analyst.
  7. The Tester and the Project Manager sit together.
  8. U, who is the Accountant, sits one place to the left of the Tester.

How many people are seated between the Developer and the Accountant in the arrangement?

In a town, there are 1,200 households. The households are classified according to their preference for different types of energy sources: Solar, Wind, and Hydro. The following statistics are provided:

30% of the households prefer Solar energy.

40% of the households prefer Wind energy.

30% of the households prefer Hydro energy.

15% of the households prefer both Solar and Wind energy.

12% of the households prefer both Wind and Hydro energy.

8% of the households prefer both Solar and Hydro energy.

5% of the households prefer all three energy sources.

The town council wants to know:

How many households are there that prefer exactly two types of energy sources?

What percentage of households prefer only one type of energy source?

Between May 1 and May 4, four books — Echoes, Flares, Gravity, and Nimbus — were each completed on a different day. The books had varying lengths of 100, 200, 300, and 400 pages.
  • The book with 400 pages was finished one day before “Flares”.
  • “Echoes” was finished after “Nimbus”.
  • “Echoes” has 200 pages.
  • The book with 100 pages was finished on May 1.
  • The book finished on May 2 is either the 200-page book or “Flares”.
When was the book Gravity published?

At a celebration, the host Anand Pathak decided to present return gifts to his guests. He selected a variety of items: Ring, Dress, Chocolates, Jewellery, Wallet, and Shoes to gift to six guests, Shaurya, Rhea, Divya, Mitali, Kabir, and Sneha not necessarily in the same order.
These gifts were placed one above the other in an almirah consisting of six shelves, numbered 1 (bottom) to 6 (top).

The following details are known:
  • The Dress, meant for Sneha, was placed on a shelf with an odd number. 
  • Divya’s gift was kept immediately above the Ring, which was located on shelf number 4. 
  • Kabir’s gift was placed adjacent to the gift chosen for Sneha.
  • The Shoes were positioned above the Ring, but they were not meant for Divya.
  • The Chocolates, which were given to Mitali, were not placed on the second shelf.
  • The Wallet, a gift for Rhea, was not kept on the third shelf.
Which of the following was placed exactly between the gift of Rhea and Shoes?

Four musicians—Tara, Usha, Varun, and Zoya—each performed solo at a weekend music fest. They played different instruments (Guitar, Drums, Violin, and Keyboard), each gave a unique performance lasting 30, 40, 50, or 60 minutes, and drew different audience sizes: 100, 110, 120, or 130 people. 
  • Usha, the one who played for 120 people, and the 110-audience performer are all different.
  • The Violin performance lasted 50 minutes.
  • Tara played the Guitar.
  • The 120-audience performer, Zoya, and Tara are three different musicians.
  • Zoya’s audience was 20 fewer than the 40-minute performer.
  • The 120-audience act was either Keyboard or the 50-minute one.
  • The longest show had 10 fewer people in the audience than the Keyboard act.
  • The drums player had 10 more people in the audience than the Violin player.
Which instrument had the largest audience?

  • If a student scores more than 90% in Assignments + Project, they get a 5% bonus added to their final average grade.
  • If the weighted average before the bonus is below 50%, the student automatically fails, regardless of the bonus.
What is the minimum score the student must get in the Final Examination to pass the course (i.e., reach a weighted average of at least 50%)?
If the student scores 88 in the Final Examination, does the student qualify for the 5% bonus? What is their final average including bonus, and did they pass?

Seven athletes – A, B, C, D, E, F, and G – each participated in two different events: Sprint and Long Jump. Their performance scores in each event are unique and range from 1 to 7, such that no two athletes have the same score in any event.
  • Only E scored identically in both Sprint and Long Jump.
  • D's score in Sprint is 4 more than C's score in Sprint.
  • Only B and C have the same total score when both events are added.
  • The total score of D is exactly double that of G.
  • The Sprint score of B is equal to the Long Jump score of F.
  • The combined score of F across both events is 11.
  • At most two athletes have a lower Long Jump score than E.
  • Long Jump score of C is exactly double her Sprint score.

What is the difference between Sprint score of D and Long Jump score of G?

Riya, Teena, and Zoya decide to invest in a business together. Riya invests Rs. 12,000 for 3 years at an interest rate of 7% per annum. Teena invests Rs. 18,000 for 2 years at an interest rate of 5% per annum. Zoya invests Rs. 25,000 for 1 year at an interest rate of 6% per annum. Find out how much Teena earns if they decide to split the total interest in the ratio of their investments in one year.

Now they decided to continue with the same amount of investments 

 But this time after one year, the business showed promising growth. So Zoya reinvests an additional Rs.15,000 into the business at the beginning of the second year and invested the same at the beginning of the third year. Teena withdraws Rs.6,000 from her initial capital at the beginning of the second year and invested the same at the beginning of the third year. Riya keeps her investment unchanged for 3 years. The total profit at the end of 3 years is now Rs.54,000, and it is to be distributed based on the weighted investment × time contribution for each person. What is Teena’s final share of the profit?

Three bookstores – Novel Nest, Page Turners, and Read Hub – sell three types of products: fiction books, non-fiction books, and magazines.
  • The number of fiction books sold by Novel Nest is 20% more than the number of fiction books sold by Page Turners.
  • The number of magazines sold by Page Turners and Read Hub is in the ratio of 2:1.
  • The number of fiction books sold by Read Hub is 40% of the total number of fiction books, non-fiction books, and magazines sold by Read Hub.
  • The number of non-fiction books sold by Page Turners is 300, which is 60 more than those sold by Read Hub.
  • The number of magazines sold by Novel Nest is 37.5% of the number of non-fiction books sold by Read Hub.
  • The number of non-fiction books sold by Novel Nest is <inlineMath>54\frac{{14}}{{59}}\% </inlineMath>of the total number of products sold by Novel Nest.
  • The total number of magazines sold by all three bookstores together is 270.
  • The total number of products sold by Page Turners is 475% of the number of magazines it sold.
What is the ratio of the number of products sold by Novel Nest and Read Hub?

A company manufactures and sells three types of air purifiers: Basic, Advanced, and Premium.
Sales Breakdown in a Quarter:
40% of the units sold were Basic models.
35% were Advanced models.
The rest were Premium models.
A total of 2,000 units were sold that quarter.
Price and Discount Details:
  • The Basic model has a base price of Rs. 5,000 and was sold with a 10% discount.
  • The Advanced model has a base price of Rs. 8,000 and was sold with a 15% discount.
  • The Premium model has a base price of Rs. 12,000 and was sold with a 25% discount.
Returns, Repair and Replacements:
  • 5% of Basic units were returned due to filter malfunction, and a full refund was issued.
  • 4% of Advanced units were repaired due to electric wire malfunction. It was repaired free of cost incurring a loss to company which is 50% of the selling price.
  • Only 1% of Premium units were returned, but instead of refunds, customers were given replacement units, incurring a production loss of Rs. 7,000 per unit.
What was the total revenue before returns (after discounts)?
What was the total loss due to returns, repair and replacements?
What was the net revenue after considering discounts and losses?

On a direct course along the river, three villages, River end, Bridge cross, and Stream Ville, are in succession, with Bridge cross being halfway between River end and Stream Ville. The total distance from River end to Stream Ville is 500 km. A Speedboat begins at 9:00 AM from River end towards Stream Ville at 100 km/h. An hour later, a boat that takes people fishing departs from Stream Ville for River end at 80 km/h. Meanwhile at the same time, a jet ski departs from Bridge cross, traveling towards River end at 60 km/h.
How far from River end do the fishing boat and speedboat pass each other? 
When and where does the speedboat overtake the jet ski?

options.text: 322.22 km, 10:56:15 AM, 193.75 km from Bridge cross
325.25 km, 10:06:15 AM, 306.25 km from Stream Ville

What is the shortest distance of Ravi’s home and ABC Science Institute from Meena’s home?

To convert a number from octal to binary we need to convert octal to decimal first. Then the decimal part is converted to the binary part. Octal number is with base 8,decimal number is with base 10 and binary number is with base 2.
To convert octal to a decimal manually, you should first start multiplying the octal numbers by 8. Then, you raise it to a power of 0 and increase that power each time by 1 according to the octa decimal equivalent system. An example to convert octal to decimal is as follows:
<inlineMath>{123_8} = \left( {1 \times {8^2} + 2 \times {8^1} + 3 \times {8^0}} \right) = 64 + 16 + 3 = {83_{10}}</inlineMath>
To convert a decimal number to binary, Divide the decimal number by 2. Note the remainder (0 or 1). Divide the quotient obtained in the previous step by 2 again. Repeat previous steps 2 and 3 until the quotient is 0. Write the remainders in reverse order (from the last remainder to the first). This sequence of 0s and 1s is the binary equivalent of the decimal number. An example to convert octal to decimal is as follows:
<inlineMath>{83 \div 2 - Quotient - 41 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{41 \div 2 - Quotient - 20 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{20 \div 2 - Quotient - 10 - Remainder 0}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{10 \div 2 - Quotient - 5 - Remainder 0}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{5 \div 2 - Quotient - 2 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{2 \div 2 - Quotient - 1 - Remainder 0}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{1 \div 2 - Quotient - 0 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
Now the remainders in reverse order (from the last remainder to the first) is 1010011
<inlineMath>{83_{10}} = {1010011_2}</inlineMath>
Convert the octal number 7365₈ into its binary equivalent.

Six film directors, Pranav, Kabir, Ritvik, Sahil, Tarun, and Uday, premiered their films at a global film festival held across six different months: February, April, July, September, November, and December. Each film belonged to a different genre: Drama, Thriller, Science Fiction, Documentary, Romance, and Animation. The premieres took place in different countries: England, South Africa, New Zealand, France, Netherlands, and Australia. The information below describes the sequence of events, but not necessarily in order.

The following are some facts about the events: 
  1. Ritvik's film premiered in South Africa, but it was not a Drama or Animation film.
  2. Pranav’s film premiered in Australia, and Tarun’s in New Zealand, but neither of them directed a Thriller or Documentary.
  3. The premiere held in the Netherlands took place in the month with the fewest days.
  4. The Science Fiction film premiered in April, but it was not in Australia.

  7. Uday directed the Thriller, but it didn’t premiere in July.
  8. Kabir’s film did not premiere in New Zealand or England.
  9. The Documentary film was premiered in France. 
Which among the following is the genre of the film of the one whose film was premiered in July?

Concerns over social media's impact on mental health have grown in recent years. According to experts, constant exposure to algorithmically-chosen photos and idealised lifestyles can cause anxiety, low self-esteem, and sadness, especially in teenagers, even if it allows people to express themselves and stay connected. Many users unintentionally create a disconnect between perception and reality by contrasting their real lives with the filtered lives they see online. Excessive screen usage has been linked in studies to emotional exhaustion, sleep problems, and stress symptoms. 

Due to these psychological repercussions, experts have called for digital well-being education and mental health support networks in schools and colleges.

 

Based on the passage, does the author present a supporting or opposing view on the impact of social media on mental health?

options.text: Supporting – The author emphasises how social media enhances connections and well-being.
Opposing – The author highlights the harmful effects of social media on mental health.
Supporting – The author encourages the use of social media for better mental health management.

questions.questionText:
In the competitive landscape of the electronics industry, customer support capability has emerged as a critical differentiator. With rapid technological advancements and increasingly complex devices, customers now demand quick, knowledgeable, and personalised assistance. Brands that offer strong post-purchase support, such as timely responses, multichannel accessibility, efficient warranty handling, and technical troubleshooting tend to build higher trust and loyalty.

Conversely, inadequate customer service can lead to user frustration, negative reviews, and brand switching. In many cases, the perception of product quality is directly influenced by the effectiveness of customer support. As electronics evolve, customer support must transition from reactive helpdesks to proactive knowledge-sharing hubs integrated with AI and self-service tools.

Which of the following arguments would most strongly support the author’s position in the passage?

options.text: Electronics companies should focus only on product innovation and leave support to third-party vendors.
Superior customer support enhances user satisfaction and helps retain customers in a competitive market.
Most customers do not expect after-sales service for electronics, so it's unnecessary.
The quality of a device alone determines long-term customer loyalty, not the support system.

questions.questionText:
The invention of the burger is a story shaped by migration, innovation, and changing food habits. While minced beef has been consumed for centuries, the idea of placing it between pieces of bread emerged in the United States during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Several towns, including New Haven in Connecticut and Seymour in Wisconsin, lay claim to the first modern hamburger. Early burgers were basic, simply a seasoned beef patty between slices of bread or a bun, but they quickly became popular due to their portability and satisfying taste.

With the rise of fast-food restaurants in the mid-20th century, burgers transformed into a symbol of American convenience culture. Globalisation further spread their popularity, leading to a wide variety of adaptations around the world. From vegetarian and vegan options to gourmet versions topped with exotic ingredients, the burger has evolved beyond its humble origins. Today, it represents not just a meal, but a global culinary phenomenon reflecting cultural preferences and innovation.

Which of the following best summarises the passage?

options.text: The evolution of the burger mirrors cultural globalisation and culinary adaptation over time.
The exact origin of the burger remains disputed among American cities, highlighting regional pride.
The burger’s journey reflects the commercialisation of food during the rise of fast-food industries.
Though humble in origin, the burger’s modern form illustrates the effects of industrialisation on eating habits.

questions.questionText:
The British East India Company (EIC) was established in 1600 as a trading company; however, it performed an essential function in the British colonisation of India. Initially, the organisation traded in spices, textiles, and different items; however, over the years, it acquired political and naval power to manipulate big territories in India.

The business enterprise’s rule had both positive and negative impacts. On the one hand, it brought modern-day infrastructure, railways, a postal system, and structured legal machinery, contributing to India’s long-term development. It also facilitated global trade, making India a key part of the British imperial economic system.

On the other hand, the EIC was ordinarily driven by profit, frequently exploiting India's resources for the benefit of the British. Heavy taxation, financial rules favouring British industries, and oppressive land sales systems caused pervasive poverty and economic distress. The organisation additionally suppressed local industries and aggravated numerous famines due to its exploitative regulations.

Which of the following is an argument in support of the British East India Company’s rule in India?

options.text: It introduced modern infrastructure like railways and a legal system
It imposed high taxes and drained India’s resources.
It suppressed local industries and caused economic distress.
Its exploitative policies contributed to widespread poverty.

questions.questionText:
Venice, the enchanting city of canals, masks, and timeless beauty, is as mysterious as it is historic. Beneath its romantic surface lies a deep tapestry of legends, secrets, and unanswered questions that have captivated travellers and historians for centuries. The city’s maze of narrow alleyways and fog-covered waterways creates an atmosphere ripe for intrigue, where truth and myth often intertwine. From the legend of the haunted island of Poveglia, once a quarantine zone and plague hospital, to whispered tales of secret societies meeting in candle-lit palazzos, Venice is a city that guards its secrets well.

The Carnival masks, now symbols of festivity, once served to conceal identity and social class, allowing citizens to indulge in behaviours otherwise forbidden. Stories of ghostly gondolas, lost treasure beneath the lagoon, and cryptic codes in ancient Venetian buildings continue to stir imaginations. Even the city’s slow sinking into the sea adds to its mystique; an eternal place fading into time. Whether it’s the silent passage of a gondola at midnight or the faded frescoes of a forgotten church, Venice remains a city where the line between reality and legend is delightfully blurred. Its mysteries are not just tales of the past; they are part of its living, breathing soul.

Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: While Venice is admired for its visual beauty and cultural heritage, its deeper appeal stems from the enigmatic blend of legend, secrecy, and the haunting passage of time.
Venice’s unique architecture and carnival traditions alone have allowed it to retain historical significance despite its gradual submersion.
The passage reveals that Venice's image as a mysterious city is largely manufactured for modern tourism and lacks historical grounding.
Venice has transitioned from a place of myth to one of rational urban decline, where facts now replace the need for stories and speculation.

questions.questionText:
In a recent environmental report, scientists warned about the accelerating pace of deforestation in the Amazon rainforest. The study, conducted over the past decade, reveals that large-scale logging and agricultural expansion has contributed to a drastic decrease in biodiversity levels. Experts emphasise the need for stricter conservation policies and sustainable land-use practices to mitigate the impact of deforestation. The findings highlight the urgency of global cooperation in addressing environmental degradation.
Identify the error and select the correct usage based on the passage.

options.text:
Error: The phrase ‘large-scale logging and agricultural expansion has contributed’ has a grammatical error.
Correct Usage: ‘large-scale logging and agricultural expansion have contributed’

Error: The phrase ‘stricter conservation policies’ should be softened to avoid bias.
Correct Usage: ‘enhanced conservation guidelines’

Correct Usage: ‘reduce the impact of deforestation.’
No error in the passage; it is correct as written.

questions.questionText:
Roman mythology was an important part of everyday life in ancient Rome, blending early Italian beliefs with strong influences from Greek mythology. The Romans borrowed many Greek Gods but gave them Latin names like Zeus becoming Jupiter and Aphrodite becoming Venus, and shaped them to reflect Roman values such as discipline, duty, and loyalty to the state. These myths weren't just stories; they helped explain the world around them, taught people how to live with honour, and even gave rulers a sense of divine support. 

As the Roman Empire grew, mythology helped bring people together by creating common rituals and symbols across different regions. But over time, with the rise of Christianity and its adoption as the official religion, these old beliefs started to fade. Still, the stories, characters, and lessons of Roman mythology didn’t disappear; they continued to shape Western literature, art, and politics for centuries, showing just how powerful and lasting those ancient tales really were.

Which of the following best illustrates a cause-and-effect relationship implied in the passage regarding Roman mythology’s influence?

options.text: The adoption of Greek deities into Roman mythology diluted original Roman religious beliefs, weakening their cultural identity.
The Roman Empire’s expansion institutionalised mythology as a political tool, strengthening imperial cohesion across diverse populations.
Christianity's rise led to the immediate abandonment of Roman mythology, eliminating its impact on future generations.
Roman myths existed independently of political motives and were unaffected by social or territorial changes.

questions.questionText:
In an age of rapid technological advancement and shifting global landscapes, lifelong learning has emerged as not just an educational ideal but a personal and professional necessity. Lifelong learning refers to the continuous, voluntary, and self-motivated pursuit of knowledge throughout one’s life. The mindset behind lifelong learning is rooted in adaptability, curiosity, and resilience. In a world where industries evolve and job roles are frequently redefined, those who are willing to learn, unlearn, and relearn are better positioned to thrive. 

Institutions, governments, and employers are increasingly recognising the value of this mindset. Initiatives such as online courses, workplace training programs, and community learning centres reflect a growing commitment to nurturing learning ecosystems beyond traditional classrooms. Ultimately, lifelong learning is not merely about acquiring facts it is about cultivating a flexible, growth-oriented approach to life that equips individuals to meet the challenges and opportunities of an ever-changing world.

Which of the following best summarises the central message of the passage on lifelong learning?

options.text: Lifelong learning is a professional trend primarily driven by employers and government policies to keep up with technological demands.
Lifelong learning involves formal schooling over an extended period and is most useful for those in rapidly changing job sectors.
Lifelong learning is a continuous and self-directed pursuit that enhances adaptability, well-being, and engagement in a dynamic world.
Lifelong learning replaces the need for traditional education and focuses solely on online courses and vocational skills.

questions.questionText:
Robert Frost was a renowned American poet whose work left an enduring mark on 20th-century literature. Born in 1874, Frost rose to prominence with his ability to depict the simplicity of rural life while weaving in profound philosophical and emotional themes. He often drew inspiration from the natural landscapes of New England, using them not just as settings, but as symbols of life’s greater questions, choices, struggles, isolation, and resilience.

Frost’s genius lay in his use of traditional verse forms and conversational language to express complex human experiences. Unlike many modernist poets of his time who experimented with free verse, Frost preferred structure, using rhyme and metre to lend formality to ordinary speech. Poems like ‘The Road Not Taken’, ‘Birches’, and ‘Mending Wall’ reflect this approach on the surface simple, yet layered with ambiguity and introspection.

His unique style made poetry accessible to a broader audience, without sacrificing intellectual depth. This rare combination of clarity and complexity earned him four Pulitzer Prizes and invited readers to reflect on their own lives through his poetic lens. Frost’s contribution was not just literary but cultural; he bridged the gap between academic poetry and the general public, making him one of America's most beloved literary voices.

What is the most likely reason Robert Frost’s poetry became widely appreciated across diverse audiences?

options.text: His poetic exploration of existential dilemmas within a structured form resonated with readers seeking meaning in everyday life.
His avoidance of universal human themes made his poetry uniquely individualistic and difficult to interpret.
His consistent use of rural settings limited the cultural reach of his work but intrigued regional readers.
His rejection of tradition and embrace of fragmented forms appealed primarily to modernist critics.

Which of the following arguments would most strongly support the author’s position in the passage?

questions.questionText:
Roughage, or dietary fibre, is often an overlooked yet vital component of a balanced and nutritious diet. Unlike other nutrients that are broken down and absorbed by the body, roughage passes through the digestive tract largely intact. Its primary role is to add bulk to stool and promote regular bowel movements, thereby preventing constipation and maintaining digestive health. However, the benefits of roughage extend beyond digestion.
Soluble fibre helps regulate blood sugar levels by slowing the absorption of sugar and also lowers cholesterol by binding to it in the digestive system. Insoluble fibre, found in foods like whole grains, bran, and vegetables, supports the movement of material through the digestive system and increases stool bulk. A high-fibre diet is associated with a reduced risk of chronic diseases such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and certain types of cancer.
In modern diets dominated by processed and refined foods, the natural fibre content is often stripped away, increasing the risk of digestive issues and long-term health complications. Reintroducing fibre-rich foods like fruits, vegetables, legumes, and whole grains not only supports gut health but also contributes to a feeling of fullness, which aids in weight management. Therefore, including adequate roughage in daily meals is not just a matter of digestion, but a cornerstone of preventive health care.
Which of the following options best summarises the central theme and idea in the passage?

options.text: While roughage contributes to digestion and regular bowel movements, its impact on broader health issues remains limited and requires further evidence.
The importance of roughage lies not only in digestive regulation but also in its role in long-term health management, particularly in fibre-deficient modern diets.
Although processed foods lack roughage, advancements in modern nutrition have made it easier to substitute fibre with dietary supplements and synthetic alternatives.
A high-fibre diet primarily benefits individuals with digestive issues; however, for the average person, its role in chronic disease prevention is largely overstated.

questions.questionText:
Modern art frequently questions conventional views of originality and beauty with its striking forms, abstract concepts, and unusual techniques. When exposed to contemporary art, students are introduced to new ways of thinking and expressing themselves. It challenges children to interact with ambiguity, symbolism, and multiple interpretations to move beyond the superficial aspects. Modern art is intellectually challenging and highly personal since it invites the observer to co-create meaning rather than providing a fixed reality.

Students who actively study modern art in the classroom, whether through painting, installations, or digital expression, tend to grow more confident in their creative ability and critical thinking skills. They discover that expression is not necessarily linear or logical and that not all problems have a single answer. This mentality change has even been connected to enhanced scientific problem-solving, technological innovation, and social empathy. Modern art transforms from aesthetics to an instrument for change as pupils view the world with greater imagination and curiosity.

 

Based on the passage, what deeper implication does the influence of modern art have on students’ broader learning and behaviour?

options.text: It makes them prefer art over science in their career choices.
It enhances their ability to memorise academic facts through visual aids.
It cultivates a mindset that supports innovation, empathy, and interdisciplinary thinking.
It restricts their thinking to only abstract and artistic domains, reducing logical reasoning.

questions.questionText:
Global health is a field dedicated to improve health outcomes and achieving equity in health for people worldwide. Its purpose goes beyond treating individual diseases; it seeks to understand and address the interconnected factors, social, economic, political and environmental that influence health across borders. In an increasingly globalised world where the spread of infectious diseases like COVID-19 or the impact of climate change can quickly transcend national boundaries, global health initiatives are essential for collective well-being.

The importance of global health lies in its collaborative approach. Countries, organisations, and communities work together to share knowledge, build health infrastructure, and respond to crises such as epidemics, malnutrition or lack of access to clean water. These efforts not only protect the vulnerable population but also create more stable, resilient societies. Investing in global health fosters innovation, strengthens international partnerships, and promotes a more just and sustainable world. Ultimately, global health reminds us that improving one community’s health contributes to the health of all humanity. 

Which of the following best summarises the central idea and tone of the passage?

options.text: Criticises global health as a tool of control, with a sceptical tone.
Highlights global cooperation to improve health, with an optimistic tone.
Argues global health lacks local impact, in a negative tone.
Describes past epidemics without proposing solutions, in a neutral tone.

questions.questionText:
In 1929, the stock market crash triggered a severe economic downturn known as the Great Depression. Businesses collapsed, unemployment soared and millions of people struggled to afford basic necessities. The widespread panic and loss of confidence in the financial system led to a sharp contraction in consumer spending and investment. As a result, the government implemented large-scale public works programmes and financial reforms to stabilise the economy. These measures aimed not only to revive economic activity but also to prevent future market collapses.
Select the primary cause and effect in the given scenario.

options.text:
Cause: The stock market crash of 1929
Effect: Millions of people struggled with basic living expenses.

Cause: High unemployment and financial struggles
Effect: The economy continued to deteriorate in the absence of any intervention.

Cause: Lack of business regulations
Effect: The stock market experienced rapid growth, and the economy stabilised.

Cause: Government intervention in the economy
Effect: The stock market crash deepened the economic losses, leading to further market collapses.

questions.questionText:
Customs and excise duties have historically played a critical role in India's fiscal framework by serving as significant sources of revenue while simultaneously acting as instruments of economic regulation. Customs duties, levied on imports and exports, are primarily designed to manage trade flows, protect domestic industries from global competition, and ensure compliance with international agreements. By adjusting customs tariffs, the government can encourage or discourage the consumption of certain goods, influence the balance of trade, and support Make in India-type initiatives.

Excise duties, on the other hand, were traditionally imposed on the manufacture of goods within the country. Though the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) has included many excise duties, specific products such as petroleum, tobacco, and alcohol still fall under excise taxation due to their unique regulatory and revenue considerations. These duties help the government maintain control over sectors with potential health or environmental impacts while generating critical funds for public welfare.

Which of the following most accurately summarises the core idea of the passage regarding customs and excise duties in India?

options.text: Customs and excise duties, although partially restructured by GST reforms, continue to serve as policy levers for maintaining economic control and addressing sector-specific challenges.
The gradual decline in the relevance of excise duties and the rise of global trade have reduced the impact of traditional fiscal tools like customs duties on India’s revenue model.
While customs and excise duties were once vital, their current role is largely symbolic, with minimal influence on national economic strategies or trade regulation.
Customs and excise duties are increasingly being replaced by broader tax reforms, thus limiting their scope to luxury and sin goods with little broader economic consequence.

questions.questionText:
Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) have emerged as a disruptive force in the digital economy¸ enabling artists, creators, and collectors to buy and sell unique digital assets. Built on blockchain technology, NFTs provide verifiable ownership of digital items such as art, music, videos, and virtual goods. One of the major advantages of NFTs is that they empower creators to monetise their work directly, often with smart contracts that provide royalties on future resales. NFTs also allow collectors to own one-of-a-kind digital assets in a world where replication is effortless.

NFTs also come with notable drawbacks. The environmental impact of blockchain networks, especially those using energy-intensive proof-of-work systems, has raised sustainability concerns. The NFT market is highly speculative, with fluctuating values and the risk of financial loss. Issues like copyright infringement, fraud, and lack of regulation also pose significant challenges. While NFTs offer exciting possibilities for digital ownership and innovation, they also raise important ethical, economic, and environmental questions that must be carefully considered. 

Based on the passage, which of the following can be reasonably inferred about the future of NFTs?

options.text: Although NFTs introduce innovative methods for creators to monetize digital assets, their future relevance will likely depend on whether technological and policy advancements can address current issues such as energy consumption, intellectual property violations, and speculative trading risks.

NFTs are expected to achieve mainstream adoption across all sectors of the economy, as their blockchain-based features ensure complete security, fairness, and long-term economic stability regardless of current drawbacks.

Given the concerns around copyright, fraud, and high energy usage, NFTs are likely to remain limited to niche digital art communities and will eventually be replaced by more eco-friendly and legally secure technologies.

The rise of NFTs marks a permanent shift in digital culture, one that will render traditional art ownership, copyright protections, and financial regulations obsolete, as decentralized systems become universally accepted and trusted.

questions.questionText:
William Wordsworth, one of the central figures of English Romanticism, revolutionised poetry by turning away from the lavish language and rigid forms of the 18th century. Instead, he embraced simplicity, emotion, and nature as the heart of poetic expression. Born in 1770, Wordsworth’s deep connection with the natural world became the cornerstone of his poetic vision. He believed that nature was not only a source of beauty but also a moral and spiritual guide, capable of healing the human soul and awakening profound truths.
Wordsworth's collaboration with Samuel Taylor Coleridge on Lyrical Ballads in 1798 marked a defining moment in literary history. In this collection, he argued that poetry should reflect the language of ordinary people and the experiences of everyday life. His most famous works, such as Tintern Abbey and Ode on Intimations of Immortality, explore themes of memory, childhood, loss, and the sublime power of nature. His verses, infused with sincerity and reverence, continue to inspire generations with their quiet strength and philosophical depth.
Which of the following statements best supports the viewpoint expressed in the passage about William Wordsworth’s contribution to poetry?

options.text: Wordsworth’s emphasis on natural imagery and emotional depth made poetry more accessible and meaningful to the common reader.
Wordsworth’s rejection of traditional poetic forms weakened the structural beauty and discipline of classical poetry.
True poetry should maintain its complexity and elevated diction to distinguish it from everyday speech.
By simplifying language and focusing on nature, Wordsworth diminished poetry’s potential to explore deeper intellectual themes.

questions.questionText:
English literature has journeyed over centuries, reflecting the changing instances, values, and voices of society. It started with Old English, a language barely recognisable to modern readers, in works like Beowulf, in which testimonies of heroism and myth ruled. This period changed into observed usage of Middle English, wherein writers like Geoffrey Chaucer, together with his Canterbury Tales, started to shape extra relatable characters and social observation. 

The Renaissance generation introduced a burst of creativity led by literary giants like William Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe. Themes of love, strength, betrayal, and human nature took the middle stage, and drama flourished. The richness of language and exploration of the human situation made this era unforgettable.

From historic epics to postmodern narratives, English literature has evolved into a rich mosaic, with each era including new colours, voices, and meanings to the tapestry of human expression.

 

Which of the following best summarises the passage on the evolution of English literature?

options.text: English literature started with Old English poetry and eventually gave rise to modern science fiction and fantasy genres.
English literature has remained largely traditional in style and content, with few significant changes in theme or structure.
From ancient myths to modern diversity, English literature has evolved by adapting to changing historical, social, and cultural contexts across centuries.
English literature was dominated by British authors until the 20th century, when American literature began to take over completely.

questions.questionText:
The discovery of penicillin by Alexander Fleming in 1928 revolutionised medicine, leading to the development of antibiotics that could effectively treat bacterial infections. The mass production of penicillin during World War II saved countless lives and marked the beginning of the antibiotic era.
